_note: Tech ages in order. The run starts in the first; raising a building with ages_up (the Bronze moot, then the Stone keep) moves the town into the next; begins = what the story says the new age brings. Buildings, map nodes, item bases and tool sets with an age only appear once the town has reached it. tools = group upgrades bought with goods while building (one each per run): gather_mult speeds gathering, carry adds to what a gatherer brings back, build_rate adds to craftsperson work speed, attack/hp add to each member's stats, field_mult adds to the food worked fields bring in, metal means their hits pierce bronze shields, steel means they also cut through mail. trader = a caravan that visits during the build phase once its building stands; each good has a price in shells and how many it brings each round. hearth_ground = the ground the age lays for good on every open square round the hearth out to hearth_ground_radius as it begins ("path" for a dirt path, or a road id from data/town.json), never lowering better ground already there.

bronze.name: Bronze age
bronze.begins: copper in the hills, tin by the dens, and traders from the south

medieval.name: Medieval age
medieval.begins: bog iron in the marshes, charcoal and steel, and room for a real town

bronze_picks.name: Bronze picks and sickles
bronze_picks.text: Tribespeople gather 50% faster and carry 1 more.

bronze_spears.name: Bronze spears and shields
bronze_spears.text: Warriors hit 3 harder, have 12 more HP, and pierce bronze shields.

iron_ploughs.name: Iron ploughs and axes
iron_ploughs.text: Tribespeople gather 50% faster, carry 1 more, and worked fields bring in twice the food.

mail_and_halberds.name: Mail and halberds
mail_and_halberds.text: Warriors hit 5 harder, have 20 more HP, and their steel cuts through mail and shields.

trader.name: Southern caravan
trader.text: Traders from the south sell tin and a little cassiterite, plus timber and dressed stone, at a steep markup over what your own people bring in.
